# Asset sources

For licences, receipts and credits of third-party assets, and where free game art, icons, palettes, plugins and animations come from.

## Core

- Licences: CC0 needs nothing (credit is a courtesy). CC-BY and OGA-BY need the credit the author asks for. BY-SA and GPL make the derived asset carry the same licence; GPL art in a closed game needs the user's decision. NC never goes into paid, monetised or commercial work. Quote a custom or unclear licence verbatim to the user rather than summarising it.
- Each grabbed asset gets a receipt `<asset-id>.json` beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`, `attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a line in the project's `CREDITS`: title, author, source URL, licence.
- `voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` searches Poly Haven (CC0 textures, HDRIs, models), ambientCG (CC0 materials, HDRIs), Kenney (CC0 packs), game-icons.net and Incompetech; `voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` saves under `assets/<source>/<id>/` with the receipt and the `CREDITS` line. Poly Haven asks that users are told its assets come from Poly Haven.
- Kenney (kenney.nl): CC0 whole packs (2D, 3D, UI, audio, textures); search matches pack names and categories only. Packs include `License.txt`.
- Animated CC0 sets: Quaternius [Ultimate Animated Character Pack](https://quaternius.com/packs/ultimatedanimatedcharacter.html) and [Ultimate Animated Animal Pack](https://quaternius.com/packs/ultimateanimatedanimals.html), Kenney [Animated Characters Protagonists](https://kenney.nl/assets/animated-characters-protagonists), and three.js [RobotExpressive](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/tree/dev/examples/models/gltf/RobotExpressive). fal’s [Meshy](https://fal.ai/models/meshy/v7.1/image-to-3d/api) `meshy/v7.1/image-to-3d` auto-rigs generated humanoids with `enable_rigging: true`; animation presets use `enable_animation: true` and `animation_action_id`.
- game-icons.net: CC BY 3.0 (a few authors CC0), credited per icon's author. Each SVG is a black square path under a white icon path; recolour or drop them via `fill`.
- Incompetech: Kevin MacLeod's music, CC BY 4.0 with his credit text; fetch single tracks only.
- Lospec: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json` returns name, author (sometimes empty; the palette page names the creator) and hex colours. Credit "<palette> by <author> (Lospec)".
- Godot Asset Library: keyless JSON at `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (without `godot_version` it returns nothing); `cost` holds the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`. Plugins and scripts, not art. The new Godot Asset Store (beta, no public API) is replacing it.
- OpenGameArt: no API. Search pages (`/art-search-advanced?keys=…`) only; robots.txt sets a 10 s crawl delay and disallows `/search/`. Licences (often several, including SA and GPL) and the attribution text are on each content page.
- Mixamo: Adobe's terms forbid access other than through its interface and any data mining, so the user downloads in their own browser; Voyager imports and rigs the FBX. Raw characters and animations are not redistributable.
- itch.io: no search API (every endpoint needs auth and covers your own account); tag pages have RSS (`itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-<tag>.xml`) without licences. Licences are free text per page; the user downloads, and pays where needed.

---
name: make-web-game
description: "Build and playtest browser games with three.js, Phaser, PixiJS, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas or KAPLAY."
applications:
  - id: threejs
    role: primary
  - id: phaser
    role: primary
  - id: pixijs
    role: primary
  - id: babylonjs
    role: primary
  - id: playcanvas
    role: primary
  - id: kaplay
    role: primary
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  craft: [asset-sources]
---

Ask first, unless the request or project already answers it:

- 2D or 3D? For someone new to game-making, Phaser (2D) and three.js (3D) cover
  most browser games. Voyager also supports PixiJS, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas and
  KAPLAY; any can be the better fit for what the user wants.
- Desktop, phone or both: keyboard and mouse, touch, or a gamepad?
- Where will it be hosted: Voyager, itch.io, the user's own site, or only played locally?

Know:

- Develop on a dev server such as Vite; ES modules and asset loads fail from `file://`. The
  handoff also opens by double-click: one self-contained HTML file (vite-plugin-singlefile).
- Open it in the preview pane with `preview_open` on the dev server's URL. Play it with
  `preview_click` and `preview_press`, look with `preview_snapshot`, and read state with
  `preview_evaluate`; exposing the game object on `window` makes that easy.
  `preview_recording_start` captures a gameplay clip.
- Browsers keep audio silent until the first click or key press.
- Hosted builds often live under a subpath, as on itch.io: build with relative asset paths
  (Vite `base: './'`). itch.io serves files case-sensitively, so match file name case.
- Generate characters, sprites, textures and backgrounds with make-image (mini-flows
  `game-asset-pack`, `sprite-directions`) and make them game-ready: transparent, one style,
  sprite sheets at the game's size. Draw art in code only for a prototype the user asked for
  or when no paid generation is available, and say so. Like the art, sound effects from
  make-sound and a music loop from make-music ship with the first playable, not tones
  synthesized in code. On an explicit publishing request, use publish-game for a stable
  playable Voyager link; use publish-to-itch when the user chooses itch.io. Creation and
  preview alone never authorize public publication.
- Voyager publication uses a readable game slug plus an automatic six-character random suffix,
  such as `moon-hop-a2b3c4.voyager.site`. Follow publish-game to choose the slug on first release.
  The returned link is permanent; renaming the game later changes its title only.
- A game meant to play inside an X post follows make-x-game, which adds the player card, framing
  checks, required square poster with title and "Tap to play", and a tested `?embed=1` layout.
  Voyager automatically supplies a 480×480 X player card when publishing with a thumbnail;
  X decides actual inline playback. General publishing can omit the thumbnail, but publish-game
  requires the warning "X will show a plain link card, not the playable game".
- Any website can iframe a public Voyager game using its root URL plus `?embed=1`; follow
  publish-game's embed example. Embedding does not provide a privileged Voyager bridge or
  relax the game's sandbox and static hosting restrictions.
- Voyager hosts built static output: bundle assets locally, and do not promise shared live rooms
  or an external game server on voyager.site. Shared rooms need the user's own server and a host
  that permits its connections. Free Voyager accounts allow two live games. Free, Starter, and
  accounts without a plan receive a quick, permissive AI safety check that fails open on a
  model outage or timeout. Plans above Starter skip content checks; structural bundle validation
  applies to every plan.
  Use publish-game for handling a limit or refused release without
  automatically removing an existing game or bypassing the check.
